supporting_observations.claim: During the alert window, WS-BCARTER-01 had repeated TCP connections to the internal proxy at 10.30.20.30:8080. The available connection records include sessions at 13:30:03, 13:36:22, 13:41:10, 13:46:34, 13:51:47, 13:55:57, 14:01:14, 14:06:22, and 14:09:12 UTC.

These connection records identify the proxy as the destination and report durations and byte counts, but do not identify the external HTTPS hostname or the originating endpoint process for the repeated sessions.

The evidence therefore does not establish whether the repeated sessions were the approved ChartMate updater checks or another application’s traffic; the timing alone is not enough to determine that the alerted activity was malicious or benign.

known_telemetry_limitations: The records for the repeated sessions are Zeek connections to the explicit proxy; they contain no external destination hostname or URL. See, for example, T005-00098, T005-00148, and T005-00205.
The supplied records do not associate those repeated proxy connections with an endpoint process. For example, T005-00148 and T005-00205 report network flow details but no process identity.

The provided evidence does not include proxy CONNECT or inspected-request records corresponding to the repeated sessions, so their destinations and content cannot be checked against the approved ChartMate updater.
claims_not_established: Which external hostnames or URLs the repeated sessions reached.
Which process initiated the repeated sessions and whether it was ChartMate’s updater.
What data, if any, was exchanged inside the HTTPS sessions.
Whether the repeated activity was authorized or malicious.
additional_evidence_needed: Proxy CONNECT and, where available, SSL-inspection records matching the repeated sessions by timestamp and client source port, including requested hostnames and URLs.
Endpoint process-to-network telemetry for WS-BCARTER-01 matching the repeated sessions.
Evidence of whether ChartMate Imaging and its updater were installed and running on WS-BCARTER-01, including updater configuration or logs for the alert window.
unrelated_findings: At 13:27:31 UTC, before the alert window, dllhost.exe performed a registry SetValue for HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Shell Folders\Common Startup. This is outside the alerted activity; the record alone does not establish persistence or maliciousness. (T005-00070)
